methodological_rigor.justification: Exemplary multi-modal study combining esiRNA screening of 45 tRNA modifying enzymes, shRNA validation across multiple patient-derived (MM117, MM011) and murine (B16F10, M1014) melanoma lines, syngeneic/xenograft models in both immunocompetent (C57BL/6) and immunodeficient (NOD-SCID) mice with CD4/CD8/NK depletion rescue experiments, RNA-seq, ribosome profiling, polysome profiling, LC-MS tRNA modification quantification, RIP-seq, spatial transcriptomics, TCGA-SKCM validation (n=473), and mass spectrometry of protein aggregates. Appropriate controls and double-knockdown rescue (shRIG-I, shHRI) experiments support causality. Statistical methods include parametric/non-parametric tests with normality checks.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study (cell lines, syngeneic mice, TCGA correlations) - Oxford LoE 5. Clinical translational relevance is strong because it identifies OSGEP/t6A tRNA modification as a novel therapeutic target for converting 'cold' melanomas to 'hot' immune-infiltrated tumors, with a prognostic gene signature validated in TCGA-SKCM cohort (survival correlation) and spatial transcriptomic data from 2 patients. Limitations noted: systemic OSGEP inhibition risks GAMOS-like pleiotropic effects.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are detailed with ethics approval numbers (ULiege #2268; NHS IRAS 216310 REC 16/LO/2098), animal housing conditions (22±2°C, 40-60% humidity, 12h light/dark), tumor size endpoints (1 cm3 maximum), antibody catalog numbers, shRNA sequences in Supplementary Dataset 7. Randomization and blinding described where possible. Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary referenced. Some ARRIVE items like formal sample size justification explicitly not performed ('No statistical methods were used to predetermine sample size').

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies a previously unrecognized mechanistic axis: t6A tRNA modification (via OSGEP) controls tumor proteostasis, which prevents ANN codon mistranslation, stress granule formation, RIG-I activation by endogenous tRNA ligands, and downstream T-cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity. This links three distinct fields (tRNA modification biology, integrated stress response, innate immune sensing) in a novel way. RIG-I activation via host tRNAs in stress granules as a mechanism for cold-to-hot tumor conversion is a significant conceptual advance.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is well-structured with logical progression from unbiased screen to mechanism to in vivo validation to patient correlation. Figures are comprehensive (Fig 1-6 plus many supplementary), with model schematic (Fig 6i) summarizing the proposed mechanism. Abstract clearly articulates findings. Some dense technical sections but overall clarity is strong and publication-appropriate.

key_strengths: Unbiased esiRNA screen of 45 tRNA modifying enzymes identifying OSGEP as top proteostasis hit in two patient-derived melanoma lines
Comprehensive immune causality established via syngeneic/NOD-SCID comparison plus CD4/CD8/NK depletion rescue experiments

Mechanistic chain: t6A loss -> ANN codon mistranslation -> protein aggregates -> HRI/eIF2a/stress granules -> RIG-I activation -> T-cell recruitment, with double-knockdown rescues (shRIG-I, shHRI) at each node
Multi-omics integration: ribosome profiling, polysome profiling, LC-MS tRNA modification quantification, RIP-seq, aggregate proteomics, spatial transcriptomics
TCGA-SKCM (n=473) validation with prognostic gene signature and spatial transcriptomic patient correlation
key_concerns: Spatial transcriptomics limited to only 2 patients, constraining generalizability of the OSGEP-T-cell proximity correlation
Therapeutic translation limited by GAMOS-associated neuronal/renal phenotypes from KEOPS inhibition, as authors acknowledge
No multiple testing correction reported for some analyses; sample sizes for certain staining experiments (n=3 tumors for RIG-I) are small
Direct small-molecule OSGEP inhibitor demonstration absent; therapeutic concept relies on genetic models
chief_reviewer.rationale: Highly novel, mechanistically rigorous multi-system study linking tRNA modification to tumor immunity via an unexpected RIG-I/stress granule axis with patient relevance - fits Tier 1 (Nature/Cell-tier) with minor revisions.
